title: How do you construct a square with a side of six centimetres?
description: A square PQRS with a side of six centimetres is constructed with a ruler and a protractor, one perpendicular at each end of PQ. Keeko raises the doubt that a ruler should be read from its very end.
teaching_notes: One idea: draw one side, raise a perpendicular at each end, cut each at the side length, then join the free corners. Watch for children who measure from the end of the ruler instead of from the zero mark.

source: How would you construct a square with a side of 6 cm? A square PQRS of side length 6 cm is constructed.
video_script.why: The child builds a square from its properties: four equal sides and four right angles, drawn with a ruler and a protractor.
video_script.substitution: A square PQRS with a side of 6 cm, drawn from the side PQ.
video_script.anchor: A square PQRS with PQ at the bottom, P at the bottom left and a ruler and a protractor beside it
video_script.wrong_answer: start measuring from the very end of the ruler
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks we should start measuring from the very end of the ruler, as the ruler begins there. On a ruler the zero mark sits a little way in from the end, so a line measured from the end comes out too short, and the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Square P Q R S is constructed, with every side six centimetres and every angle ninety degrees.

final_answer.value: square PQRS with PQ = QR = RS = SP = 6 cm and all angles 90 degrees
final_answer.spoken: square P Q R S is constructed, with every side six centimetres and every angle ninety degrees

never_show: the finished square before the answer
maths_rules: A square has all 4 sides equal and all 4 angles 90 degrees.
Draw PQ = 6 cm with the zero mark of the ruler at P.
At P, place the protractor with its centre at P and its baseline along PQ, mark 90 degrees and draw the perpendicular through P; mark S on it with PS = 6 cm.
At Q draw the perpendicular to PQ and mark R on it with QR = 6 cm; a compass with its opening kept at 6 cm can be used instead.
Join R and S; check RS = 6 cm and the angles at R and S are 90 degrees.
The finished square has PQ = QR = RS = SP = 6 cm.
video_script.design: One idea: a square is built from one side and two perpendiculars. Uses the two properties of a square. Wrong idea: measure from the end of the ruler. The square stays all video.
